hypothesis: A regime-aware execution router that predicts return magnitude (not just direction) and dynamically selects maker vs taker based on predicted net edge vs all-in cost will achieve positive risk-adjusted net executable expectancy on BTCUSDT 10s order-flow data. V14 proved order-flow has ranking information (AUC 0.666) but zero economic value because (a) the model predicted direction not magnitude, and (b) the confidence gate filtered out almost all trades. V15 directly predicts return magnitude and only trades when predicted return exceeds all-in cost + safety margin.
scientific_basis: V14: AUC 0.666 direction ranking, but return calibration bins all negative — model ranks but cannot predict magnitude
V14: 10s BTC returns std = 2.26 bps, mean ~0 — execution cost 3.25 bps exceeds typical return
V15 directly predicts return magnitude (regression) instead of calibrating from direction bins
Regime filter (high vol + high liquidity) concentrates trades where order flow has stronger signal
Maker execution reduces cost floor to 0.25 bps entry; taker only when predicted return > taker cost
Safety margin: require predicted return > all-in cost + 1.0 bps buffer

architecture.features: 10 order-flow features (reuse V14) + 3 regime features (vol, liquidity, spread)
architecture.execution_router: Dynamic maker/taker selection based on predicted return vs cost thresholds
architecture.regime_filter: Only trade in high-vol (top 50%) AND high-liquidity (top 50%) regimes

data_rules: V14 data is EXCLUDED from calibration
Forward capture must start AFTER calibration ends
Model frozen before any forward data is seen
